title: Rabbi Shiyan
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rabbi Acha’s student, citing [Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.6.3), “Rabbi Shiyan taught before Rabbi Acha.”

At the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.2.2), Rabbi Shiyan reports that Rabbi Acha’s eye ranged over the whole Torah and did not find it (he searched the whole Torah for a place where “labors” is written and did not find it).

He is mentioned at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 3, and Eruvin 6:6. His precious saying remains to us in [Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bikkurim.3.3.17): “Rabbi Shiyan said: One who is appointed [judge] for money — one does not rise before him, one does not call him Rabbi, and the cloak upon him is like a donkey’s saddlecloth.” See also the entry Rabbi Ashyan.

notes.text: The first series is Jerusalem Talmud. The paid-appointment saying, refusal to call him Rabbi and donkey-saddlecloth comparison preserve the supplied negative clauses; no identity is inferred from the cross-reference.

Guggenheimer Bikkurim 3:3 directly names Shiyan and preserves the two refusals and donkey-saddlecloth comparison. The cross-reference to Ashyan is not an identity determination, and other chapter/halakhah occurrences remain separate.

The consulted Hebrew calls him Shiyan in all three passages. Guggenheimer’s English uses Ashian in [Eruvin 1:6:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.6.3), [Shabbat 7:2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.2.2), and [Bikkurim 3:3:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bikkurim.3.3.17).
